description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of different relational association categories evaluated in the MMRA benchmark for large visual language models, with each slice corresponding to a specific relation type and its frequency (count and percentage) across the dataset. The chart contains ten distinct categories, each labeled with its name, count, and percentage of the total. The largest segment is “NearSameEntity” with 126 instances (12.28%), followed by “SimilarMaterial” (106, 10.33%), “SubEvent” (100, 9.74%), and “UsageSimilarity” (100, 9.65%). Other categories include “Environment,” “Layout,” “AppearanceSimilarity,” and “SimilarEvent,” each with 90 instances (8.77%); “MentalitySimilarity” with 89 (8.67%); “RelativePosition” with 81 (7.90%); and “NearSameEntity” (a smaller segment, possibly mislabeled or duplicated in labeling) with 63 (6.34%). The slices are color-coded and arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top-left, with percentage values and counts displayed inside each segment. No legend is present, but the labels are directly attached to their respective slices, making the chart self-contained for interpretation. The visual emphasis on “NearSameEntity” as the largest slice suggests it is the most frequently occurring relation type in the benchmark.
